candidate_rule: two non-promoted candidates per record: verified fact and explicit scope guard

scope_guards.c: Ofcom annual market and usage statistics are aggregate or historical observations and do not prove current speed, availability or orderability for an exact address.
scope_guards.l: National coverage predictions, programme targets and funded-delivery totals are aggregate evidence and do not establish current parcel-level connectivity.
scope_guards.g: The government address checker is planning evidence with supplier-dependent updates and an explicit accuracy disclaimer; no exact-address result was queried or promoted.
scope_guards.o: ONS local-statistics metadata and aggregated indicators do not provide an exact-address service determination or confidence interval.

documents.title: Levelling Up Missions annual report 2025 to 2026

records: The Communications Market Report 2026 was published by Ofcom on 30 June 2026.
The report describes the Communications Market Report as an interactive data portal combining industry data, Ofcom consumer research and selected third-party headline figures.
The UK telecoms sector generated £34.7 billion in revenue in 2025.
UK telecoms-sector revenue decreased by £0.3 billion year on year in 2025.
The year-on-year decrease in UK telecoms-sector revenue was 0.8% in 2025.
Retail fixed services generated £14.9 billion in revenue in 2025.
Retail mobile services generated £14.5 billion in revenue in 2025.
Wholesale fixed and mobile services accounted for the remaining £5.3 billion of telecoms-sector revenue in 2025.
Mobile services accounted for 49.4% of total retail telecoms revenue in 2025.
Mobile services' share of retail telecoms revenue increased by 0.2 percentage points compared with 2024.
There were 29.3 million UK fixed broadband connections at the end of 2025.
UK fixed broadband connections increased by 126,000 compared with 2024.
Full fibre supplied 42% of UK broadband connections at the end of 2025.
The full-fibre share of UK broadband connections increased by 11 percentage points year on year.
There were 12.3 million full-fibre lines at the end of 2025.
The number of full-fibre lines increased by 3.4 million in 2025.
Full-fibre line count increased by 38% in 2025.
There were 9.9 million fibre-to-the-cabinet connections at the end of 2025.
Fibre-to-the-cabinet connections declined by 2.6 million during 2025.
There were 1.3 million ADSL lines at the end of 2025.
The number of ADSL lines fell by more than one quarter during 2025.
Average monthly data use per residential fixed broadband connection was 583 GB in July 2025.
Average residential fixed-broadband data use increased by 52 GB per month compared with July 2024.
Average residential fixed-broadband data use increased by 10% year on year.
Average monthly residential fixed-broadband data use was 531 GB in July 2024.
There were 21.4 million UK fixed voice connections at the end of 2025.
UK fixed voice connections decreased by 2.8 million year on year.
UK fixed voice connections decreased by 12% year on year.
Other fixed voice lines, mainly managed VoIP connections, reached 12.9 million at the end of 2025.
Other fixed voice lines increased by 1.4 million in 2025.
Other fixed voice lines increased by 12% in 2025.
Total fixed and mobile voice call volume was 164 billion minutes in 2025.
Total fixed and mobile call volume fell by 12 billion minutes in 2025.
Total fixed and mobile call volume fell by 7% in 2025.
Outgoing calls from fixed lines totalled 15 billion minutes in 2025.
Outgoing fixed-line call volume fell by 19% in 2025.
Outgoing calls from mobile phones totalled 149 billion minutes in 2025.
Outgoing mobile call volume fell by 6% in 2025.
Mobile networks originated 91% of fixed-and-mobile call volume in 2025.
Mobile networks originated 90% of fixed-and-mobile call volume in 2024.
There were 123 million UK mobile subscriptions at the end of 2025.
UK mobile subscriptions increased by 4% year on year.
Machine-to-machine subscriptions increased by 4.1 million in 2025.
Post-pay subscriptions represented 82% of UK mobile subscriptions in 2025.
The post-pay share increased by one percentage point year on year.
There were 101 million post-pay mobile subscriptions in 2025.
There were 22 million pre-pay mobile subscriptions in 2025.
Average monthly data use per mobile data user reached 11.8 GB in 2025.
Average monthly data use per mobile data user increased by 1.1 GB in 2025.
Average monthly data use per mobile data user increased by 11% in 2025.
Average monthly mobile data use across all mobile users was 10.7 GB in 2025.
Average monthly data use across all mobile users increased by 11% year on year.
Average outgoing call volume per mobile subscription was 146 minutes per month in 2025.
Average outgoing call volume per mobile subscription fell by 6% in 2025.
Average outgoing messages per mobile subscription were 21 per month in 2025.
Average outgoing messages per mobile subscription fell by around one quarter in 2025.
Average monthly post-pay customer call use was 164 minutes in 2025.
The Levelling Up Missions annual report 2025 to 2026 was published on 13 July 2026.
The report's mission-progress summary covers January 2025 to January 2026.
The digital-connectivity mission states that the UK should have nationwide gigabit-capable broadband and 4G mobile coverage by 2030.
The mission states an ambition for higher-quality standalone 5G to extend to all populated areas.
Predicted 4G coverage from at least one operator remained at 96% of UK landmass in January 2026.
The reported 4G landmass coverage from at least one operator was unchanged from January 2025.
Overall 5G coverage from at least one operator reached 73% of UK landmass in January 2026.
Overall 5G coverage from at least one operator had been 62% of UK landmass in January 2025.
Overall 5G landmass coverage from at least one operator increased by 11 percentage points between January 2025 and January 2026.
Overall 5G was available outside 98% of UK premises in January 2026.
Overall 5G was available outside 96% of UK premises in January 2025.
Standalone 5G from at least one operator covered 59% of UK landmass in January 2026.
Standalone 5G from at least one operator was available outside 93% of UK premises in January 2026.
Gigabit-capable coverage reached 88% of UK premises in January 2026.
Gigabit-capable coverage had been 84% of UK premises in January 2025.
The January 2026 gigabit-capable coverage level exceeded the interim target of 85% by 2025.
The government now expects to deliver nationwide gigabit broadband by 2032.
More than 80 Home Office masts were upgraded during the reporting period for the Shared Rural Network.
Total investment in the extended 5G Innovation Regions programme rose to £46 million.
Government-funded programmes had upgraded more than 1.3 million rural and harder-to-reach premises to gigabit-capable broadband by the end of December 2025.
The BDUK gigabit-broadband availability guidance was first published on 13 March 2026.
The guidance was last updated on 7 July 2026.
The address-checking service is intended for addresses in England and Wales.
The service reports whether gigabit broadband is available or planned for an address.
The guidance directs users in Scotland to a separate Scottish broadband checker.
The guidance directs users in Northern Ireland to a separate Northern Ireland service.
The address checker used data from the January Open Market Review published in June 2026.
The next address-checker data update was scheduled for September 2026.
The address-checker data is intended to be updated every four months.
The guidance states that supplier plans can change and complete accuracy of an address's gigabit status cannot be guaranteed.
The ONS gigabit-capable broadband indicator measures the percentage of premises covered by a service offering download speeds of 1,000 Mbps or more.
The indicator describes UK coverage as of January 2026.
Ofcom is the data source for the ONS gigabit-capable broadband indicator.
The ONS indicator was published on 13 May 2026.
The indicator includes data only for January 2026.
Confidence intervals are not available for the indicator.
The map, bar chart and table use lower-tier or unitary-authority geography.
ONS provides the indicator for download in CSV, CSVW and XLSX formats.
ONS warns that some indicator data has been aggregated and may differ from other published figures.
ONS links the original source data for the indicator back to Ofcom.
